headline: HIGH-GRADE GOLD: McFarlane Lake Hits 6.58 g/t Au Over 10m at Juby 826 Zone — Geophysics Points to 1.6km Trend
snippet: McFarlane Lake Mining returned 6.58 g/t Au over 10.35m within a broader 3.32 g/t Au over 22.35m interval at the Juby Gold Project's 826 Zone in Ontario's Abitibi Greenstone Belt. New 3D IP geophysical modelling suggests the 826 trend may extend 1.6km northwest toward the Golden Lake deposit — opening a priority new corridor outside the existing resource.

headline: SILVER OUTPACES GOLD: Spot Surges 2.62% to $77.50 on Iran-U.S. Diplomacy — Gold-Silver Ratio Compresses to 58.9
snippet: Silver hit $77.50/oz Monday (+2.62%), handily outpacing gold which held at $4,521/oz — up $1,167 from a year ago. Trump's statement that the U.S. and Iran had "largely negotiated" a Strait of Hormuz memorandum knocked the dollar lower. The gold-silver ratio compressed to 58.9, a threshold analysts say marks convergence of industrial and investment demand for silver.

headline: 40,000 METRES LAUNCHED: Contango Fires Up 5 Deposits at BC's Golden Triangle — Resource Update Due H1 2027
snippet: Contango Silver & Gold launched its 40,000m 2026 program at the Kitsault Valley project in BC's Golden Triangle with three diamond drills now turning on Torbrit and North Star — two more coming online within the week. The campaign covers six deposits including Homestake Ridge, with a new resource estimate and preliminary economic study targeted for H1 2027.

headline: GOLCONDA GOLD DEBT-FREE: New Mexico's Summit Mine Set to Start Mining by End of Q2 — 50,000 oz Target by 2028
snippet: Golconda Gold's Q1 2026 results confirm the fully permitted Summit Mine in New Mexico's Steeple Rock District is weeks away from first ore with processing expected in H2. The company has cleared its debt and is targeting 50,000+ gold-equivalent ounces annually by 2028, with Summit planned to spin out as a standalone U.S. gold-silver producer in Q4 2026 or early 2027.

headline: PECOY COPPER UNLOCKS GOLD UPSIDE: Phase 1 Metallurgy Flags Step-Change Recovery Potential at Peru Cu-Au-Mo Project
snippet: An independent Phase 1 metallurgical review of Pecoy Copper's Peru copper-gold-molybdenum-silver project identified significant room to improve gold recovery while maintaining marketable copper concentrate grades. The review re-examined historical test work through a broader payable-metals lens — a potential re-rating catalyst if the improvements confirm at scale.

headline: USA RARE EARTH (USAR) EXAMINED: Pentagon Contracts, Round Top Heavy RE Deposit — Can the Mine-to-Magnet Bet Pay Off?
snippet: The Motley Fool scrutinizes USA Rare Earth (USAR), which aims to be one of America's first mine-to-magnet rare earth businesses. The company owns the polymetallic Round Top heavy rare earth deposit in Texas, an operational magnet factory in Oklahoma, and growing Pentagon contract exposure — all as China's quarterly concentrate pricing hits a seventh consecutive rise.

headline: MAY 29 DEADLINE: Zijin Gold's C$5.5B Allied Gold Takeover at Final Hurdle — Mali Mines Confirmed Running
snippet: Allied Gold has confirmed its West African operations are running normally as the May 29 contractual outside closing date arrives for Zijin Gold International's C$5.5 billion friendly all-cash takeover. The C$44/share offer — a 27% premium over the 30-day VWAP — is awaiting final regulatory approvals, making this one of the largest gold M&A transactions to close in 2026.

headline: ZIMBABWE CUTS OFF LITHIUM: Export Ban Squeezes 7% of Global Supply as China Carbonate Surges to Two-Year Highs
snippet: Zimbabwe's suspension of all raw mineral and lithium concentrate exports has tightened a market that was already squeezed by Chinese lepidolite mine halts. Zimbabwe accounts for roughly 7% of global lithium output and 15% of China's spodumene imports. Battery-grade lithium carbonate in China surged to CNY 200,500/t — the highest in two years — before easing to CNY 191,000/t, having roughly doubled from December 2025 lows.

headline: BEYOND ELECTRIC TRUCKS: Mining's Path to Net Zero Demands Integrated Systems, Not Bolt-On Fixes
snippet: A Metal Tech News op-ed published today argues that piecemeal electrification — swapping out diesel equipment one item at a time — misses the deeper systemic opportunity in mining's net-zero transition. The piece contends that meeting decarbonization targets requires integrated mine system design, energy orchestration, and data-driven operations working together rather than in isolation.

headline: TUNGSTEN GOES STRATEGIC: GoldHaven Repositions BC's Magno Project as Non-Chinese Critical Mineral Supply
snippet: GoldHaven Resources is highlighting tungsten-bearing skarn systems and indium exposure at its 37,200-hectare Magno project in BC's Cassiar region as Western governments accelerate critical mineral supply chain investments. The 2026 program will include airborne geophysics and drill-testing of tungsten, silver-lead-zinc CRD, and porphyry copper-molybdenum targets across the land package.
